hints: Look at Ivan's and Oscar's statements. Neither one is about the lights: each says that someone else is lying.
Ivan's statement is the opposite of Lena's, and Oscar's is the opposite of Ivan's. So Lena and Oscar are both truthful or both fibbing.
If Lena and Oscar both fibbed, Nadia would need to be truthful, naming Oscar, and that makes Lena's statement true. So Lena and Oscar are truthful.

solution.key_idea: Ivan contradicts Lena and Oscar contradicts Ivan, so Lena and Oscar stand or fall together, and they must be the two truthful ones.
steps: Ivan says Lena is lying, so Ivan's and Lena's statements are opposites. Oscar says Ivan is lying, so Oscar's statement matches Lena's.
If Lena and Oscar both fibbed, Ivan's would be the only true one of the three, so Nadia's would have to be true.
Then Oscar did it, so neither Nadia nor Lena did, and Lena's statement would be true after all. That cannot be.
So Lena and Oscar tell the truth, and Ivan fibs. That makes two true statements, so Nadia fibs too.
Lena's statement clears Nadia and Lena, and Nadia's fib clears Oscar. So Ivan unplugged the lights.
solution.epilogue: Ivan had pulled the plug to run his cotton candy machine, sure it belonged to the closed pony ride. Gus came down with a sunny forecast and a free pink cone.
